member.name: F:ReadyM.Relay.Client.RelayClient.ExpectedStallDisconnectTimeoutMs
member.summary: How long a stall is tolerated while one is expected. Bounded, so a transition that never finishes still gets noticed, just later than usual.

member.name: F:ReadyM.Relay.Client.RelayClient.TrafficResumedSilenceMs
member.summary: Silence short enough to mean packets are flowing again. One ping interval, so it clears as soon as the peer is genuinely talking to us.

member.name: F:ReadyM.Relay.Client.RelayClient.TrafficResumeGraceMs
member.summary: How long to keep waiting for traffic after a stall ends. If nothing arrives by then the connection really is gone, so hand the timeout back and let it say so.

Monotonic clock for the grace period above.

member.name: M:ReadyM.Relay.Client.RelayClient.BeginExpectedStall
member.summary: Raises the disconnect timeout while a known stall is in flight, so the stall does not count against it. Paired with .

member.name: M:ReadyM.Relay.Client.RelayClient.RestoreDisconnectTimeoutWhenTrafficResumes
member.remarks: The silence counter only advances while the network loop runs, so right after a stall it is still catching up on the time that passed. Restoring then would re-arm the short timeout on a peer that is already most of the way through it, and the next tick would report a timeout on a connection that is actually fine. So wait for a packet to prove traffic is flowing.

member.name: T:ReadyM.Relay.Client.Utilities.NetworkSessionStats
member.summary:
All-time network session stats: - Ping distribution via fixed histogram [0..MaxValidPingMs] (exact percentiles) - Packet loss (ping > MaxValidPingMs) + streak severity - Upload/Download rate in bytes/sec computed from LiteNetLib NetStatistics deltas (exact percentiles via stored samples)
Not thread-safe by design (we use a single network thread).
